text: {"findings":[{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Unsourced churn and cost figures","detail":"The 12% never-reorder rate and $48M annual cost are cited only as 'industry data' with no specific source, and the $48M is not tied to LMD's own volume.","evidence_quote":"Industry data shows that 12% of customers never reorder after a late delivery, costing roughly $48M a year.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the specific source for both figures and derive the $48M from LMD's own late-delivery and reorder data."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Guardrails miss reorder and abuse risks","detail":"The proposal adds a credit incentive but its only guardrail is Cost Per Delivery. It has no guardrail on credit abuse or fraud, no on-time delivery or courier impact guardrail, and no reorder or retention measure, even though reorder loss is the stated problem.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: stop if it rises by more than $0.15.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for credit redemption and abuse rate, order refund or contact rate, and on-time delivery rate. Track reorder rate as a success or guardrail metric."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric does not match the stated problem","detail":"The problem is lost reorders, but the success metric is CSAT on late orders. This is a survey-based metric that is likely subject to response bias, since credited customers may respond differently. No reorder or retention metric is defined.","evidence_quote":"Delivery CSAT on late orders: baseline 3.6, target 3.9 within 8 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use canonical glossary metrics such as 30-day reorder rate for late-delivery customers as primary, and define how CSAT response bias is handled."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Duration under 14 days of effect and mismatch with target timeframe","detail":"The 3-week run is inconsistent with the 8-week target window. Outcomes depend on a next order that occurs after the credit is applied, and many late-delivery customers will not reorder within the 3 weeks. Randomizing by customer is acceptable, but the design is not powered to measure reorder behavior.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by customer. Duration: 3 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Extend the experiment to cover the reorder window, or align the metric timeframe with the run length. Compute the sample size for the reorder-rate MDE."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Only informing Finance, no approval recorded","detail":"The credit is a monetary customer payment with financial impact, and the proposal only says Finance was 'informed'. No formal Finance approval is recorded, and no review of credit and fraud policy is mentioned.","evidence_quote":"Finance has been informed of the expected credit volume.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record explicit Finance and policy approval for the credit program, including the credit value and budget."}]}
